mechanism: Intravenous L-citrulline is an amino-acid precursor of arginine and nitric oxide intended to improve nitric-oxide bioavailability, vasodilation, and blood flow during sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06989567 as a not-yet-recruiting, randomized, quadruple-masked Phase 3 study of IV L-citrulline plus standard-of-care pain management versus placebo plus standard of care in 120 patients aged 6 to 21 years with sickle cell disease presenting to emergency departments with acute vaso-occlusive crisis. Estimated start is 2025-07-25, estimated primary completion is 2027-06, estimated study completion is 2029-06, and no results are posted. FDA's orphan-drug database lists L-citrulline for treatment of sickle cell disease as designated but not FDA-approved for the orphan indication.
expected_launch_window: 2028-2030 if Phase 3 enrollment, data, filing, and FDA review are successful
clinical_summary: NCT06989567 targets acute VOC treatment in the ED, a setting where care remains largely supportive with opioids and standard pain protocols. The Phase 3 regimen is a 50 mg/kg IV bolus followed by 9 mg/kg/hour continuous infusion for up to 12 hours, with primary outcomes of change in pain score from baseline to discharge and time to pain crisis resolution. Differentiation is potentially meaningful because the candidate is positioned as an acute VOC-abortive therapy rather than chronic prevention, but current evidence is unproven: NCT06989567 has no results and the earlier Asklepion Phase 1/2A study NCT04852172 was terminated without posted results.
safety_summary: ClinicalTrials.gov describes prior pediatric SCD experience as safe and well tolerated, with rare, non-serious temporary low blood pressure. The Phase 3 trial excludes patients with hypotension requiring intervention, hemodynamic instability, septic shock, severe anemia, acute chest syndrome, sepsis, acute organ dysfunction, stroke concern, recent systemic steroids, inhaled nitric oxide, arginine, nitrates, PDE5 inhibitors, and unreliable venous access. A completed Phase 1 continuous IV citrulline study in 4 adults reported no deaths, one serious adverse event of transaminitis, and adverse-event collection through 4 weeks.
management_tools: Medical-benefit or hospital formulary protocol rather than routine pharmacy-benefit coverage
Restrict use to FDA-labeled age range, confirmed sickle cell disease, and acute uncomplicated VOC presentation if approved
Require administration in ED or inpatient monitored setting with standard-of-care pain protocol
Weight-based dosing and course limits aligned to final label, anticipated as one bolus plus up to 12 hours of infusion per qualifying VOC episode

Exclude or require clinician attestation for hypotension, hemodynamic instability, sepsis, acute chest syndrome, stroke concern, acute organ dysfunction, severe anemia, and contraindicated vasodilator or nitric-oxide pathway medications
Track pain-score response, IV opioid use, admission rate, length of stay, return visits, and adverse events
P&T review before formulary adoption because the ingredient is also sold as a supplement but the studied product is an investigational sterile IV drug formulation
evidence_gaps: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results for NCT06989567.
NCT06989567 is listed as not yet recruiting with last update posted 2025-05-29; no public confirmation of first patient enrolled was found.
Earlier Asklepion study NCT04852172 was terminated, enrolled 30 patients, and has no posted results.
No FDA approval, label, or direct price for IV L-citrulline in sickle cell disease was identified.
Annual cost uses Endari, an approved prescription amino-acid SCD therapy, as a pricing analog; it is not a direct estimate of acute IV L-citrulline episode pricing.
The eventual payer impact will depend heavily on per-episode price, average annual VOC frequency, hospital reimbursement treatment, and whether treatment reduces admissions or length of stay.

sources.title: A Study of Intravenous L-Citrulline in Patients Aged 6-21 Years Old With Sickle Cell Disease Presenting to Emergency Departments in Acute Vaso-Occlusive Crisis
supports: Sponsor is Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC and official title describes a Phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study in children, adolescents, and young adults aged 6 to 21 years.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; estimated enrollment is 120; estimated start is 2025-07-25; estimated primary completion is 2027-06; estimated study completion is 2029-06.
The trial is FDA-regulated, has a data monitoring committee, and has no posted results.
Experimental treatment is IV L-citrulline 50 mg/kg bolus followed by 9 mg/kg/hour continuous infusion for up to 12 hours plus standard-of-care pain management.
Primary outcomes are change in pain score from baseline to discharge and time to pain crisis resolution.
Secondary outcomes include duration of hospital stay, total opioid use, proportion with at least 30% reduction in opioid use, PROMIS pain interference change, and hospital admission rate.
Detailed description states L-citrulline is a natural substance/amino acid that helps the body make nitric oxide and is intended to improve blood flow in SCD VOC.

sources.title: L-citrulline Injection in Patients Aged 6-21 Years Old with Sickle Cell Disease Presenting with Vaso-Occlusive Crisis (VOC)
supports: Sponsor is Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC.
Phase 1/2A open-label dose-finding study with subsequent double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized study in SCD VOC.
Study was terminated with reason: impacted by viraemia resulting in higher than expected admissions.
Actual enrollment was 30; actual primary completion and study completion were 2024-02-29.
No results are posted.
Primary measures included dose optimization, pharmacokinetics, pain-score change, opioid use, ED/hospital discharge within 7 hours, and safety.

sources.title: A Phase 1 Study of Continuous Intravenous L-citrulline During Sickle Cell Pain Crisis or Acute Chest Syndrome
supports: Completed Phase 1 study of continuous IV citrulline in sickle cell disease.
Actual enrollment was 4; study started 2016-02 and completed 2017-04; results are posted.
Dose description was IV citrulline bolus followed by continuous infusion for 23 hours.
Adverse events were collected up to 4 weeks after study-drug administration.
Results reported no deaths, one serious adverse event of transaminitis, and four participants with adverse events.

sources.title: Pipeline - Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC
supports: Asklepion pipeline lists intravenous citrulline.
Pipeline page lists acute sickle cell crisis as an indication for intravenous citrulline.
Company states it focuses on commercializing innovative drugs for children.

sources.title: IV Citrulline - Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC
supports: Asklepion describes citrulline development as pediatric clinical research.
Company describes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 IV citrulline study in pediatric congenital heart surgery.
Background states citrulline supplementation may increase plasma citrulline and arginine concentrations.
This supports that Asklepion is developing IV citrulline as a pharmaceutical program, though the page is focused on cardiopulmonary bypass rather than SCD.

supports: Generic name is L-citrulline.
Orphan designation is treatment of sickle cell disease.
Designation status is designated.
FDA orphan approval status is not FDA approved for orphan indication.
Sponsor is Asklepion Pharmaceuticals, LLC.

sources.title: Design of an adaptive randomized clinical trial of intravenous citrulline for sickle cell pain crisis in the emergency department
supports: The article states VOC is the most frequent cause for ED visits and hospital admissions in SCD.
The article states nitric oxide plays a critical role in vaso-occlusion pathogenesis and citrulline is an endothelial nitric-oxide booster.
The described trial aimed to determine IV L-citrulline pharmacokinetics, optimal dose, efficacy, and tolerability in children and adolescents with SCD presenting to the ED in VOC.
Endpoints included pharmacokinetic parameters, pain scores, opioid-use reduction, quality of life, hospital admission proportion, readmission rates, and adverse events.

sources.title: DailyMed: ENDARI (glutamine) powder, for solution
supports: Endari is an amino acid indicated to reduce acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and pediatric patients 5 years and older.
Dose is 5 g to 15 g orally twice daily based on body weight.
Each packet contains 5 g of L-glutamine powder.
Adverse reactions reported in more than 10% of Endari-treated patients include constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremity, back pain, and chest pain.
Use is supported by two placebo-controlled studies in adult and pediatric SCD patients.

sources.title: Emmaus Life Sciences Provides Additional Operational and OTC Markets Updates
supports: Emmaus stated Endari WAC per box was $1,110 in 2019.
Emmaus stated Endari WAC per box increased to $1,154 effective 2020-01-01.
The company stated patient cost is reduced by applicable copay assistance and patient assistance programs.

sources.title: Endari Prior Authorization Program Summary
supports: Endari prior authorization program lists the FDA indication as reducing acute complications of SCD in adults and pediatric patients 5 years and older.
The policy notes generic availability.
The policy describes VOC as the most common acute complication of SCD and notes SCD can range from mild to requiring frequent hospitalizations.
The policy supports the use of diagnosis- and indication-based payer controls for amino-acid SCD therapy.

expected_launch_window.value: 2028-2030 if Phase 3 enrollment, data, filing, and FDA review are successful
expected_launch_window.method: Used estimated Phase 3 start, primary completion, study completion, absence of results, and FDA orphan status showing no current SCD approval.
expected_launch_window.explanation: If the Phase 3 study starts and reads out around the 2027 primary completion estimate, a successful filing and FDA review could plausibly support launch from 2028 onward; delays are possible because the trial remains not yet recruiting and final study completion is estimated for 2029.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Endari as the closest priced prescription amino-acid SCD analog. Endari WAC was $1,154 per 60-packet box effective 2020-01-01; labeled dosing is 2 to 6 packets/day. Annualized WAC = 365 days x 2 or 6 packets/day / 60 packets per box x $1,154, rounded to whole dollars.
annual_cost_range.explanation: No direct IV L-citrulline price is public. This analog likely overstates or misaligns with a single acute IV course because Endari is chronic oral therapy, but it provides a source-backed amino-acid SCD price range until per-episode IV pricing is disclosed.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted the acute ED/VOC-abortive positioning, nitric-oxide pathway rationale, Phase 3 status, and endpoints focused on pain, IV opioid use, hospitalization, and length of stay against the lack of posted efficacy results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: An IV therapy that shortens acute VOC, reduces opioid use, or avoids admissions would be clinically meaningful versus supportive care, but differentiation remains prospective until Phase 3 data are available.

budget_impact.method: Assessed targeted episodic use in a rare disease, potential hospital/ED administration, unknown price, analog amino-acid SCD annual WAC, and possible offset from reduced admissions or length of stay.
budget_impact.explanation: Population size and episodic use limit broad spend, but hospital implementation, uncertain pricing, and acute-care utilization create enough uncertainty for a Medium rating.

disruption_risk.method: Rated operational disruption from ED/inpatient protocol changes, need for monitored IV administration, clinical exclusions, potential opioid and admission impacts, and current evidence immaturity.
disruption_risk.explanation: If approved, L-citrulline would require acute-care pathway work rather than routine specialty-pharmacy edits, but data and launch timing remain uncertain.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to not-yet-recruiting Phase 3 status, no posted results, no direct price, and orphan-designated but not approved regulatory status.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor trial activation, enrollment, data release, FDA filing, labeling, and pricing. Begin protocol planning only when Phase 3 efficacy and operational value are clearer.

quality_flags: L-citrulline is a naturally occurring amino acid and common nutritional-supplement ingredient; the assigned record is nevertheless an FDA-regulated investigational sterile IV drug study sponsored by Asklepion.
Non-approved orphan asset: FDA orphan database lists L-citrulline for treatment of sickle cell disease as designated but not FDA approved for the orphan indication.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06989567 as not yet recruiting with no posted results and last update posted 2025-05-29.
Earlier Asklepion SCD study NCT04852172 was terminated and has no posted results.
Direct product price is unavailable; annual cost estimate uses Endari prescription amino-acid SCD therapy as an analog and may not reflect acute IV L-citrulline pricing.
The company IV citrulline product page is primarily focused on cardiopulmonary bypass acute lung injury, while the pipeline page and FDA orphan designation support the sickle cell disease program.
